headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Claude Code can hand sensitive local context to Perplexity’s vendor-hosted search backend, while shared filesystem/git state also enables prompt-injection and write conflicts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git, and Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can influence the other, especially if Claude Code reads files as trusted. The pathway is not fully direct, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Claude Code reads files produced by Perplexity without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or copied documents, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a provenance header to every transferred file or note.
Restrict Claude Code to a read-only review pass on imported content.
Use a dedicated transfer folder with manual approval before opening files.
Strip instructions from Perplexity outputs before feeding them to Claude Code.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance tracking between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and sends queries to api.perplexity.ai/search providers. If sensitive local files are copied into Perplexity, data can leave the host and reach a third party. The blast radius includes secrets and code, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF sensitive repo files or environment-derived secrets are pasted or uploaded into Perplexity, they can be transmitted off-host.
IF Claude Code exposes secrets in files it reads, Perplexity may receive them through copied context.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets or .env contents into Perplexity.
Use a redaction step before any upload or query.
Limit Perplexity to public or sanitized documents only.
Review Claude Code outputs for secret-bearing paths before sharing.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on the transfer path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; Perplexity cannot write locally, but it can still influence what Claude Code edits by returning code or instructions. The main conflict is on shared mutable repo state, not direct simultaneous writes, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree, Claude Code can overwrite or race with human edits.
IF Perplexity-generated patches are applied without coordination, git state can diverge.
mitigations: Serialize edits through one agent at a time.
Commit or stash before handing work to the other agent.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Review diffs before applying Perplexity suggestions.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repo operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers and browsing context that Claude Code may treat as authoritative when editing code or running shell actions. Because Claude Code has execution and git-write authority, a mistaken Perplexity answer can cascade into irreversible repo changes or unsafe commands. The default interaction is dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF Claude Code uses Perplexity output as a direct source for code or commands, errors can propagate into commits or shell execution.
IF Perplexity cites stale or incorrect web results, Claude Code may operationalize them without verification.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before execution or commit.
Ask Claude Code to cross-check Perplexity claims against primary sources.
Use Perplexity only for research, not as an action source.
Keep a checklist for commands derived from search results.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or policy gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git history, shell environment, and local files on the host, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch for code or sensitive documents, but the profiles do not specify a concrete regulated data class like PHI or EU PII, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workflow, it may be processed by a vendor-hosted service.
IF the operator requires local-only residency, Perplexity violates that expectation for uploaded content.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity prompts and uploads.
Use Perplexity only on public or de-identified material.
Document a data-handling rule for the pair.
Review vendor privacy terms before sending sensitive files.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a local-only toolchain.
